Page | U.S. Representative <span style="color: #c00000;">The Right to Bear Arms&nbsp;</span></h3> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">The Second Amendment to the U.S. Constitution affirms a right that is fundamental to a free society, which in turn depends on personal responsibility.&nbsp; As a proud Texan and gun-owner myself, I know just how important that right is.&nbsp; Indeed, it is the freedom that secures the First Amendment rights.</span></p> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">Moreover, the Second Amendment right of Americans “to keep and bear Arms” has been upheld by the Supreme Court of the United States in two significant cases: McDonald v. City of Chicago (2010) and District of Columbia v. Heller (2008).&nbsp; Those two decisions declared unconstitutional the virtual ban on the ownership of handguns imposed by Chicago, Illinois, and Washington, D.C.&nbsp; The Court reaffirmed that the Second Amendment grants an individual the right to bear arms in defense of one’s home, and that right applies to all levels of government.</span></p> <h3><span style="color: #c00000;">The Right to Life&nbsp;</span></h3> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">It is no secret that I am unapologetically pro-life.&nbsp; As a member of Congress’ Values Action Team (VAT) and the House Pro-Life Caucus, I am committed to protecting pro-life policies while pushing back on Democrat proposals to promote the so-called “pro-choice” agenda.&nbsp; I have consistently voted in support of measures to prevent abortions, as well as the use of taxpayer money for such an egregious practice.</span></p> <h3><span style="color: #c00000;">Freedom of Speech, Conscience, and Assembly</span></h3> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">The First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution guarantees that “Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof; or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a

Page | U.S. Representative </b> <h3><span style="color: #c00000;">Education</span></h3> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">I believe that all children deserve educational opportunity and a chance for future success.&nbsp; We are lucky to have such great schools, faculty, and staff in the 14th Congressional District of Texas.&nbsp; As the husband of a now-retired 4th Grade teacher, I know firsthand the hard work and dedication that our teachers and administrators invest in educating our future leaders.&nbsp; These public servants are the unsung heroes within our communities.</span></p> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">Unfortunately, ever-growing federal intervention in education has come at the expense of state and local control, has saddled teachers and school leaders with a tremendous paperwork compliance burden, and has failed to effect meaningful gains in education.&nbsp; The data shows that millions of children pass through America’s schools without receiving an education that prepares them to succeed in life and to thrive in the increasingly competitive global economy.&nbsp; America’s students need and deserve better.&nbsp; I believe it is our local schools—not some remote bureaucrats—that are best equipped to meet the needs of our schoolchildren.&nbsp; We need to restore state and local control of education to better serve students across the country.</span></p> <h3><span style="color: #c00000;"><b>Jobs</b>&nbsp;</span></h3> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">Just over two years ago, President Donald Trump signed the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) into law. &nbsp;Since then, we continue to see our economy grow through the creation of more jobs, 50-year low unemployment, and small business optimism. Our economy continues to flourish, with over 150,000 new jobs created every month in 2019. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics’ first 2020 jobs report, we surpassed last year’s numbers, adding 225,000 jobs in January alone, while holding the unemployment rate steady at 3.6 percent.</span></p> <p><

Page | U.S. Representative <span style="color: #c00000;">Energy</span></h3> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">Along Texas’ Gulf Coast, we take great pride in the diverse energy resources that we refine and ship.&nbsp; &nbsp;That pride comes not only from how energy drives our economy, but also from knowing that we contribute to making America more secure.<br /> <br /> American ingenuity and an abundance of shale gas have resulted in the United States becoming the world's largest producer of natural gas. &nbsp;And now, thanks to liquefied natural gas (LNG) export facilities like those in Texas, American energy is reaching markets around the globe.<br /> <br /> This is good news for hard-working Texans. &nbsp;It is also good news for America’s national security. &nbsp;Many of our allies around the world—ranging from South Korea to Germany—find themselves dependent on natural gas from hostile or autocratic regimes like Russia and Iran. &nbsp;With American LNG hitting the global market, our friends and strategic partners abroad will have the opportunity to supply their energy needs from the United States. &nbsp;Supporting our allies while creating good-paying jobs at home is a win-win.<br /> <br /> With 90 percent of American LNG passing through the Sabine-Neches Waterway, this issue is especially important to our district. &nbsp;That is why I’ve urged the Department of Energy to expedite the permitting process so that more LNG export facilities can quickly ramp up production to meet global demand.</span></p> <b></b> <h3><span style="color: #c00000;">The Environment</span></h3> <p style="text-align: center;"><span style="color: #1f497d;"><em>A</em></span><span style="color: #1f497d;"><em>s a father and grandfather, I agree that keeping our water, land, and air clean is important. &nbsp;Policies that promote these valuable goals must also take into account their impact on job creation and economic growth.</em></span></p> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">&nbsp;</

Page | U.S. Representative </b> <h6 style="text-align: center;"><span style="color: #1f497d;"><span style="font-size: 20px;">As a firm believer in limited government and a capitalist economy, I am very concerned about the out-of-control spending by our government, and the enormous debt future Americans will inherit.&nbsp; More government is not the answer.&nbsp; More spending is not the answer.&nbsp; More taxes are not the answer.&nbsp; The answers are found through hard choices to cut spending and to limit the government, thereby ensuring a stronger, safer America for tomorrow.</span><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp;</span></span></h6> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2><span style="color: #c00000;">Debt, Deficits, and Spending</span></h2> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">A budget <b>deficit</b> occurs when government spending is greater than the revenue collected in the same fiscal year.&nbsp; In contrast, the national <b>debt</b> is the accumulation of each year’s deficit.&nbsp; Since 1970, there have only been four years during which the federal government has not operated in deficit.&nbsp; As a result, our national debt now exceeds $26.6&nbsp;trillion, which translates into more than $80,000&nbsp;per citizen.&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">Lowering America’s debt burden is critical because when interest rates rise, the government’s debt payments will begin to crowd out other parts of the federal budget, and individuals will begin to see higher rates on mortgages, credit cards, and car loans as a result.</span></p> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">Mandatory spending—to include Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, other directed outlays, and interest payments on the debt—consumes 70 percent of all federal spending each year.&nbsp;&nbsp;In fact, interest payments on our debt have become the sixth largest category in the federal budget.&nbsp; As long as outlays continue to exceed federal receipts, resulting in annual defic

Page | U.S. Representative </b> <h3><span style="color: #c00000;">Foreign Affairs</span></h3> <p><span style="color: #c00000;">&nbsp;</span><span style="color: #1f497d;">Having served for two terms on the House&nbsp;Committee on&nbsp;Foreign Affairs, I am aware of the essential role that Congress plays in directing U.S. foreign policy.&nbsp; With our “power of the purse,” the House has a duty to restrain and punish our adversaries,&nbsp;while supporting our global allies.</span></p> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">&nbsp;</span><span style="color: #1f497d;">The global environment is changing, and America’s adversaries&nbsp;are&nbsp;increasingly acting against U.S. interests.&nbsp; Congress has worked with the&nbsp;Trump Administration to push back against military aggression&nbsp;around&nbsp;the globe.&nbsp;&nbsp;In previous years, we passed&nbsp;legislation ensuring&nbsp;that bad actors such as Iran, China, North Korea and Russia were&nbsp;confronted,&nbsp;reassuring&nbsp;America’s global allies&nbsp;of our commitment.&nbsp; In 2017, Congress passed the Countering America’s Adversaries through Sanctions Act (H.R. 3364), which strengthened sanctions on Russia.&nbsp; At a time when Russia is increasingly threatening its neighbors, including key NATO allies such as Estonia,&nbsp;Latvia&nbsp;and Lithuania, Congress must demonstrate our steadfast commitment to our friends and be willing to punish states that threaten our interests.</span></p> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">&nbsp;</span><span style="color: #1f497d;">Congress took action to support the State of Israel in the face of threats from Iran and the terrorists that it supports.&nbsp; On September 12, 2018, the House passed the United States-Israel Security Assistance Authorization Act (S. 2497).&nbsp; This act extends America’s commitment to helping Israel defend itself, including by strengthening the critical Iron Dome Missile Defense System.&nbsp; This system is al

Page | U.S. Representative <span style="font-size: 20px; color: #1f497d;"><em>I believe that all Americans should have access to affordable health care.</em> <em></em></span></h4> <h3><span style="color: #c00000;"></span><span style="font-weight: bold; color: #c00000;">Alternative Approaches</span></h3> <span style="color: #1f497d;">Obamacare has proven that it is not the solution to expand access and lower costs, which is why I support repealing the current law and replacing it with less costly and less burdensome alternatives.&nbsp; Commonsense alternatives would spur competition by allowing individuals to purchase health insurance across state lines, and it would rein in the growth of health care costs by adopting medical liability reform that protects patients and doctors from expensive lawsuits. &nbsp;Additionally, this approach would expand the ability for families and individuals to deduct their health care costs, while providing federal grants for state-based, high risk pools, and safeguarding individuals who have pre-existing conditions with limits on participants’ charges.<br /> </span><span style="color: #1f497d;"><b></b></span> <h3><span style="color: #c00000;">Prescription Drug Therapies</span></h3> <span style="color: #1f497d;"><b></b>There is no question Americans pay too much for health care, including the cost of prescription drugs.&nbsp; As you may know, U.S. prescription drug use has grown substantially during the past several decades as researchers have developed groundbreaking therapies.&nbsp; In fact, $333 billion was spent on prescription drugs in 2017 alone.&nbsp; Unfortunately, current law has restricted patient options for doctors and drugs, and bad actors have recently used a complicated regulatory system to retain a monopoly on drug supply and prevent competition in the market.&nbsp; The result is far too often financially crippling for families. </span> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">&nbsp;</span><span style="color: #1f497d;&q

Page | U.S. Representative </b> <h3><span style="color: #c00000;">Homeland Security and Immigration</span></h3> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">Homeland security is vitally important.&nbsp; To ensure our security, it is essential that we have strong borders and enforce our immigration laws. &nbsp;Texans have a strong sense of fairness.&nbsp; Unfortunately, our broken immigration system cannot be called fair.&nbsp; It is not fair to those who patiently wait in line to enter legally.&nbsp; It is not fair to American workers who must compete with illegal immigrants working for artificially low wages.&nbsp; Our broken system&nbsp;and porous borders also leave us less safe.&nbsp; Despite the tireless efforts of our Border Patrol and&nbsp;immigration enforcement officers, drugs and people continue to cross our southern border.&nbsp; We can and must make this system better.</span></p> <p><span style="color: #1f497d;">When I was in the Texas House of Representatives, I served as the Vice-Chair of the Border and Intergovernmental Affairs Committee and saw how drug and human traffickers endangered both Americans and immigrants.&nbsp;&nbsp;Until the border is secured, immigration reform will not be effective.&nbsp;&nbsp;Otherwise, lax co
